title: outer trapped surface formation from gravitational waves collision
abstract: we give a new rigorous construction of outer trapped surface formation in smooth vacuum spacetimes without symmetry assumptions. the outer trapped surface is produced by the collision of two transversely localized, nearly plane-fronted gravitational waves described by short pulse data. the outer trapped surface is obtained by joining two smooth pieces along a curve with their future-directed outer null normals matching continuously. the incompleteness of the maximal future development is then established by adapting penrose's original argument. this construction is inspired by penrose's argument in constructing a marginally outer trapped surface in the collision of two ultra-relativistic particles modeled by the aichelburg--sexl solution.

title: global isometric embedding of the kerr spacetime and beyond
abstract: we construct a new isometric embedding of the kerr spacetime into $(5+7)$-dimensional flat spacetime. it is asymptotically flat, covers the entire $r>0$ region and has a very simple form. we also show how this embedding can be generalized to any spacetime admitting a kerr-schild-like decomposition of the metric.

title: weak solutions for weak turbulence models in electrostatic plasmas
abstract: the weak turbulence model, also known as the quasilinear theory in plasma physics, has been a cornerstone in modeling resonant particle-wave interactions in plasmas. stemming from the vlasov-poisson/maxwell system under the weak turbulence assumption, incorporating the random phase approximation and ergodicity, it takes the form of a integro-differential system, which describes the time dynamics of particle distribution and wave spectrum. the interaction between particles and waves can be treated as a stochastic process, whose transition probability bridges the momentum space and the spectral space. to our knowledge, there is no preceding rigorous analytical work for the quasilinear theory addressed in this manuscript. in this paper, we establish the existence of global weak solutions to the one-dimensional electrostatic quasilinear model for nonnegative, smooth, rapidly decaying initial particle distributions and nonnegative, smooth wave spectra compactly supported in a positive wave-number band. the construction uses the resonance condition to reduce the coupled system to a scalar degenerate parabolic equation, together with uniform estimates and strong convergence of the gradients of regularized approximations. when the initial wave spectrum is positive throughout a single band, we further characterize the equilibrium selected by this approximation procedure. the equilibrium uniquely minimizes a quadratic functional over a nonnegative cone and admits a geometric construction through the least concave majorant of a primitive determined by the initial data. the limiting particle distribution is non-increasing on the corresponding resonant interval and forms plateaus wherever the equilibrium auxiliary function is positive. a relative-entropy argument establishes long-time convergence to this equilibrium.

title: sharp quartic pinching for the mean curvature flow in the sphere
abstract: we prove a sharp quartic curvature pinching for the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{s}^{n+m}$, $m\ge2$, which generalises pu's work on the convergence of submanifolds in $\mathbb{s}^{n+m}$ to a round point. using a blow up argument, we prove a codimension and a cylindrical estimate, where in regions of high curvature, the submanifold becomes approximately codimension one, quantitatively, and is weakly convex and moves by translation or is a self shrinker. with a decay estimate, the rescaling converges smoothly to a totally geodesic limit in infinite time, without using stampacchia iteration or integral analysis.

title: singular semilinear elliptic equations in half-spaces
abstract: we prove the monotonicity of positive solutions to the problem $-δu = f(u)$ in $\mathbb{r}^n_+ := \{(x',x_n)\in\mathbb{r}^n \mid x_n>0 \}$ under zero dirichlet boundary condition with a possible singular nonlinearity $f$. in some situations, we can derive a precise estimate on the blow-up rate of $\frac{\partial u}{\partialη}$ as $x_n \to 0^+$, where $(η,e_n)>0$, and obtain a classification result. the main tools we use are the method of moving planes and the sliding method.

title: a pöschl--teller approximation to the wave equation outside a torus
abstract: we prove dispersive estimates for an approximation to the wave equation in the exterior of a torus. because no separation of variables into a basis of eigenfunctions and eigenvalues exists in toroidal coordinates for the time harmonic problem, we introduce a related approximate operator for the dirichlet laplacian in the exterior of a torus. the approximate operator separates into schrödinger operators with pöschl-teller potentials after freezing $n=n_0$ in the conjugated laplacian. the operator here which we develop is related to the so-called mehler-fock kernel. using the known solution to the eigenvector and eigenvalue problem of pöschl-teller, a high-frequency analysis of the approximate operator for the wave equation can be made accurately. the operator for this problem gives an angularly truncated $l^1\rightarrow l^{\infty}$ dispersive estimate on compact coordinate collars. duhamel's principle controls its error for the corresponding exterior wave operator with dirichlet laplacian.

title: feedback stabilization and tracking for heat equations using thermo-plasmonic nanoparticles as actuators
abstract: we propose a feedback strategy to track prescribed heat profiles using plasmonic nanoparticles as actuators. starting from a thermo--plasmonic maxwell--heat model, we use a time-domain discrete effective description in which the generated heat is approximated by a superposition of heat kernels centered at particle locations with amplitudes governed by a coupled volterra system. we recast this dynamics as a heat equation on a bounded domain with finitely many point actuators and design a tracking feedback based on pointwise evaluations of $\mathcal a^{-1}y$, where $\mathcal a=i-a_0$ and $a_0$ is the neumann diffusion operator. working in the natural $v'$ setting with $v=d(\mathcal a)$, we prove exponential stabilization of the tracking error via distribution-actuator theory. for non-equilibrium reference profiles, we add a constant feedforward term and a low-mode fixed-point pre-compensation on $x_n$, ensuring exact steady matching on $x_n$ and an explicit bound on the residual tail mismatch.

title: schrödinger ultrahyperbolic equations with singular coefficients
abstract: in this paper we investigate the cauchy problem for schrödinger ultrahyperbolic equations with singular (less than continuous) coefficients. we prove $h^\infty$ well-posedness in the very weak sense under suitable assumptions of the distributional structure of the coefficients and decay on the lower order terms. consistency is proven with the classical $h^\infty$-results when the equation coefficients are smooth.

title: invariant and super-median functions for perturbed heat kernels
abstract: we study super-median and invariant functions for positive and negative schrödinger perturbations of non-negative kernels. for positive perturbations, combining dynkin's formula for the original kernel with duhamel's formula for the perturbation, we derive perturbed dynkin-type identities and give integrability conditions ensuring invariance. when the perturbed kernel is given by the perturbation series, we obtain a sufficient condition for a function to be super-median without additional integrability assumptions. we also decompose every finite non-negative solution of duhamel's equation into the perturbation series and a non-negative solution of the corresponding homogeneous equation. for negative perturbations, we obtain analogous identities under an explicit finiteness condition. we also construct functions satisfying dynkin's formula using zero-resolvents and compensated kernels. examples involving gaussian, fractional, and bessel kernels illustrate the invariance criteria and the role of non-uniqueness in duhamel's equation.

title: local well-posedness of the two-dimensional incompressible schrödinger flow
abstract: we consider the incompressible schrödinger flow (isf), an efficient model for simulating incompressible inviscid fluids introduced by chern et al. \cite{c17,ckpsw16}, on a bounded, simply connected two-dimensional domain. after transforming it into the director formulation, the equation becomes the schrödinger map (or the landau--lifshitz equation) transported by a velocity field generated from the director itself via biot--savart law. we show that the director formulation has a unique local-in-time strong solution. then, we lift the solution to the director formulation to the spinor, and conclude that it is indeed a unique solution to the isf. this result is a first rigorous analysis on isf, a widely used computational model.

title: a jost--pais theorem for the intermediate long wave equation
abstract: for a one-dimensional schrödinger operator, the transmission coefficient can be expressed as a fredholm determinant. this fundamental discovery of jost and pais has recently proven very influential in the study of conserved quantities for the korteweg--de vries equation, whose lax operator takes this form. in this paper, we obtain an analogue of this result for the intermediate long wave equation, where, startlingly, the transmission coefficient is given by a \emph{ratio} of fredholm determinants. we then recover the original jost--pais result in the shallow-water limit and its analogue for the benjamin--ono equation as the infinite-depth limit.

title: condensation and non-condensation in the quasilinear 4-wave kinetic equation
abstract: we study finite-time condensation at zero frequency for the isotropic quasilinear 4-wave kinetic equation in three dimensions. with schrodinger dispersion and a product interaction coefficient with exponent $β\in(0,3/4]$, we construct global measure solutions $(g_t)_{t\geq0}$ for every nonnegative initial measure $g_0$ with finite wave action and energy. we then establish the sharp threshold $β=1/4$ for finite-time condensation of the constructed solutions. for $β\in[1/4,3/4]$, the constructed solutions satisfy $g_t(\{0\})=g_0(\{0\})$ for all $t\geq0$. for $β\in(0,1/4)$, every constructed solution with $(g_0)_{\mathrm{ac}}\neq0$ satisfies $\|g_t-\mathcal{n}_0δ_0\|_{\mathrm{tv}}\leq c\mathcal{n}_0(1+\mathcal{n}_0^2t)^{-(1-4β)/40}$ for all $t\geq0$, where $\mathcal{n}_0=g_0([0,\infty))$ and $c=c(β,g_0/\mathcal{n}_0)>0$. in particular, for every $ζ\in(0,1)$, there exists $t_ζ<\infty$ such that $g_t(\{0\})\geq(1-ζ)\mathcal{n}_0$ for all $t\geq t_ζ$.

title: an exact mass threshold for global existence and blow-up in semilinear anti-de sitter equations
abstract: we study the influence of the mass parameter on global existence and finite-time blow-up for the semilinear anti-de sitter klein--gordon equation \[   ϕ_{tt}-e^{2t}δϕ+nϕ_t+m^2ϕ=|ϕ|^p   \qquad\text{in }[0,\infty)\times\r^d. \] after removing the damping term, we establish $l^2$ energy estimates for the resulting klein--gordon equation with constant coefficient in the potential. they imply global existence for arbitrary sufficiently small energy data, without spatial localization, whenever \(   m^2>-\frac{d(2n+d)}{4}   \quad\text{and}\quad p>1. \) in the remaining mass parameter interval above the structural threshold, an exact change to conformal time reduces the problem to a scale-invariant effective damped wave equation. exponentially weighted energy estimates then extend global existence to \(   -d(n+d)<m^2\le-\frac{d(2n+d)}4   \quad\text{for every } \quad p>1. \) in the complementary regime $m^2\le-d(n+d)$, we prove finite-time blow-up for every $p>1$ and for weak solutions with finite speed of propagation arising from nonnegative, nontrivial initial data. we further obtain lifespan estimates that are polynomial at the threshold and logarithmic below it. thus, $m^2=-d(n+d)$ is the exact structural mass parameter threshold separating the global-existence and blow-up regimes.

title: observability of wave equations with time- and space-dependent potentials: a counterexample under gcc and a positive criterion on the disk
abstract: we show that the geometric control condition (gcc) for the free wave equation does not guarantee internal observability in the presence of a smooth time-dependent potential. on a bounded connected domain with analytic boundary, we construct a nonempty open observation set such that the pair satisfies gcc and the free dirichlet wave is observable, and a smooth $2π$-periodic potential for which there exists a nonzero smooth dirichlet wave that vanishes on the observed cylinder for all time. the wave is the unique mild solution in the space $x_ω=l^2(ω)\times h^{-1}(ω)$ on every finite interval, so no finite observation horizon yields an observability inequality for this fixed potential. the construction starts from a real-valued local counterexample to unique continuation across a noncharacteristic hyperplane; this local statement is of independent interest, since earlier constructions for the wave operator use complex-valued waves and potentials. the global counterexample is obtained by joining flat oscillatory solutions along the edges of a polygonal observation set, repairing their sum at the vertices without changing its zero set, and then using a spatial transition to a common time-independent pair near the boundary.   for comparison, on the unit disk we show that an observation region containing a central disk and a neighborhood of an embedded cross-cut yields observability for every weak wave at sufficiently large observation time, with constants uniform over bounded measurable potentials; the proof uses a cut, logarithmic polar coordinates, and a carleman weight whose favorable flux is confined to the observed artificial boundary.

title: the calderón problem for quasilinear currents
abstract: we study the calderón problem for smooth quasilinear current laws on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{r}^n$, $n\geq3$. under the stated structural assumptions and analyticity conditions, the interior current law is determined by local dirichlet-to-neumann maps, up to a partial-boundary-fixing diffeomorphism and a hall-effect-type invisible current. the two obstructions come from the linearized inverse problem, which is solved by combining boundary determination for magnetic schrödinger operators with analytic continuation in solution coordinates. higher-order linearization and a boundary argument involving products of three solution gradients then determine the remaining taylor coefficients.

title: endpoint capacity at strictly stable minimal boundaries:gaussian layers and schwarzschild deficits
abstract: let $(m^n,\mathfrak g)$, $3\le n\le7$, be a one-ended asymptotically flat manifold whose boundary $σ$ is a connected, strictly stable, outermost minimal hypersurface. as $p\downarrow1$, the $p$-capacity of $σ$ converges to its area, by a theorem of fogagnolo and mazzieri. we establish a higher-order asymptotic expansion governed by a single function on $σ$: the positive solution $g$ of the reciprocal jacobi equation $jg=g^{-1}$. after a universal term, the first correction is determined by the average of $\log g$, and the capacitary potential drops from one to zero across a gaussian boundary layer of width $g\sqrt{p-1}$; under the normalized energy measure, the logarithm of the gradient has limiting variance $\frac12$ plus the variance of $\log g$. in dimension three, assuming in addition that $r_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{ii}|^2\ge0$ along $σ$, we identify the capacity deficit of $σ$ relative to the schwarzschild horizon of the same area at order $p-1$: it is nonnegative, vanishes exactly when the induced metric of $σ$ is round and $r_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{ii}|^2\equiv0$, and controls the deviation of $g$ from a constant through a relative-entropy identity.

title: blow-up of damped semilinear wave equation with short range potential and critical power nonlinearity
abstract: the present paper is devoted to the study of a semilinear wave equation with spatially dependent scattering damping and a short-range potential, with particular focus on determining the critical exponent for the power-type nonlinearity. by employing the test function method, we establish wave-type blow-up results and derive lifespan estimates at the critical level. the main contribution of this work lies in providing a uniform asymptotic analysis for a family of test functions, which is achieved through a detailed investigation of a parametric second-order elliptic equation. as a further novelty, we relax the radial symmetry condition conventionally imposed on the coefficients $d$ and $v$ by resorting to the comparison principle in conjunction with a monotone exhaustion argument.

title: one bubble against a ring: new sign-changing solutions of the brezis-nirenberg problem
abstract: we consider the brezis--nirenberg problem $-δu=|u|^{2^*-2}u+\varepsilon u$ in the unit ball of $\mathbb r^n$, $n\ge5$, with dirichlet boundary conditions, and we look for sign-changing solutions which, as $\varepsilon\to0^+$, blow up positively at the centre and negatively at the $k$ vertices of a regular polygon. the key observation is that, for this configuration, the gradient of the reduced energy factorises, so that the whole finite-dimensional problem is governed by the zeros of a single explicit function of the radius of the polygon. its behaviour depends on the dimension: when $n=5$ such solutions exist for every $k\ge2$, and the ring of negative peaks approaches the boundary at distance $o(1/k)$; when $n\ge6$ there are two solutions for $2\le k\le6$, while no solution of this type exists for $k$ large. for $2\le k\le6$ the nodal set of every such solution reaches the boundary of the ball, in contrast with what happens for the almost critical problem. nevertheless, the two solutions found for $n\ge6$ have very different nodal structures: numerically, for $3\le k\le6$ one of them has only two nodal domains, and its nodal set meets the plane of the peaks along a closed curve around the centre, while the other one can have as many as $k+1$ nodal domains. these results extend to higher dimensions a configuration previously found in dimension four.

title: absence of non-threshold embedded eigenvalues for nonlinear schrödinger equations
abstract: we consider the focusing nonlinear schrödinger equation on $\mathbb{r}^d$ \begin{equation*}   i\partial_tu+δu+|u|^{p-1}u=0. \end{equation*} we prove the absence of non-threshold embedded eigenvalues for the linearized operator around the positive ground state when $d=1,2$ and $p>1$, or when $d\ge3$ and $1<p\le1+\frac4{d-2}$. starting from the fluid variables of nls, we derive a biharmonic wave equation for the phase gradient after linearization around the ground state. seeking a virial identity for this equation, we identify a mechanism for establishing a repulsive structure, which guides the subsequent ode analysis to exclude embedded eigenvalues.

title: smooth radial quantized type ii blow-up for the three-dimensional energy-critical nonlinear schrödinger equation
abstract: we consider the focusing energy-critical nonlinear schrödinger equation in three dimensions. in \cite{schmid2026cvpde}, schmid constructed finite-time type ii blow-up solutions with a continuum of blow-up rates, while the existence of smooth finite-time type ii blow-up solutions remained open. we resolve this problem by constructing, for each integer $l\ge1$, smooth radial solutions concentrating a single ground state with the blow-up rate $λ(t)=(\ell+o(1))(t-t)^{2l}$ for some $\ell>0$.   our proof follows a forward construction based on modulation analysis with the energy method. the main obstacle is the lack of a repulsive structure that can be directly exploited to control the remainder. to overcome this obstacle, we adapt kato's smoothing theory from asymptotic stability analysis to the forward construction. this yields a global spacetime morawetz estimate for the linearized flow, providing the spacetime control needed to bound the higher-order energy in place of the monotonicity derived from repulsive structures in previous blow-up constructions.

title: critical functions and asymptotics for fractional hartree brezis--nirenberg problems in low dimensions
abstract: we study the brezis--nirenberg problem for the fractional laplacian with an upper critical hartree nonlinearity on a bounded domain $ω\subset\mathbb r^n$, in the low-dimensional range $2s<n<4s$. for a continuous potential $a$, we prove that the following properties are equivalent: the robin function of $(-δ)^s+a$ is negative somewhere in $ω$; the associated hartree--sobolev quotient ${\mathcal s_{h,s}}(a)$ lies strictly below the best constant ${\mathcal s_{h,s}}$; and ${\mathcal s_{h,s}}(a)$ is attained. this leads to the notion of a critical potential, for which ${\mathcal s_{h,s}}(a)={\mathcal s_{h,s}}$ and every nontrivial decrease of $a$ lowers the infimum. for a critical potential $a$ and $v\in l^\infty(ω)$, we determine the leading term in the asymptotics of ${\mathcal s_{h,s}}(a+\varepsilon v)$ as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ and describe the blow-up of almost-minimizers, including the concentration speed and the location of the concentration point. compared with the sobolev case, the nonlocal nonlinearity produces several new interaction terms; a key ingredient is a proof of non-attainment at the threshold based on the sharp hardy--littlewood--sobolev inequality on the sphere.

title: blow-up bounds under profile approximation for superconformal wave equations
abstract: for the focusing semilinear wave equation in the superconformal, sobolev-subcritical range, we prove an upper blow-up bound at the ode rate near a non-characteristic point, assuming approximation by signed multiples of explicit stationary profiles in similarity variables. the comparison parameters may vary with time, and the error is measured only in a degenerate energy norm on a small extension of the unit ball. the main step is a quantitative exclusion of concentration at the boundary of the profile family. it follows from the nonnegativity of the superconformal hamza--zaag energy at admissible vertices and an upper perturbation estimate. we also exclude families with an isolated dominant profile and, under a noncancellation condition, clusters of comparable profiles. for the latter, we derive a limiting energy in $\r^{n+1}$ which accounts for the interactions between profiles.

title: pointwise wave--damping for linearized vlasov--poisson: compactly supported radial equilibria and relativistic applications
abstract: we establish weighted pointwise estimates for the response green function and the complete electric field of the linearized vlasov--poisson system in $\mathbb{r}_x^3\times\mathbb{r}_v^3$ around compactly supported radial equilibria. both decompose into a dispersive wave component with $t^{-3/2}$ decay in $l_x^\infty$ and a faster-decaying landau-damped component. the wave estimate includes the survival threshold, where the oscillatory branch meets the continuous spectrum, while the damped estimates resolve the spatial fronts associated with the velocity boundaries. the equilibrium class includes shells with independent inner and outer orders of vanishing, down to first order, and profiles positive throughout a velocity ball. the proof combines a joint treatment of pole and continuum contributions with a low-frequency normal form for the electric field. the electric-field estimates hold for real, neutral perturbations with finite weighted regularity and imply uniform scattering along free characteristics. an exact momentum--velocity correspondence for suitable filled-ball profiles yields analogous estimates and scattering for a class of nonnegative relativistic equilibria with polynomial momentum tails.

title: gravitational waves from cosmic superstrings and gauge strings
abstract: we perform a phenomenological comparison of the gravitational wave (gw) spectrum expected from cosmic gauge string networks and superstring networks comprised of multiple string types. we show how violations of scaling behavior and the evolution of the number of relativistic degrees of freedom in the early universe affect the gw spectrum. we derive simple analytical expressions for the gw spectrum from superstrings and gauge strings that are valid for all frequencies relevant to pulsar timing arrays (ptas) and laser interferometers. we analyze the latest data from ptas and show that superstring networks are consistent with 32 nhz data from nanograv, but are excluded by 3.2 nhz data at $3σ$ unless the string coupling $g_s<0.2$ or the strings evolve in only about 10% of the volume of the higher-dimensional space. we also point out that while gauge string networks are excluded by nanograv-15 data at $3σ$, they are completely compatible with epta and ppta data. finally, we study correlations between gw signals at ptas and laser interferometers.

title: kerr-newman outside a rotating de sitter-type core: different types of interior electromagnetic fields and currents
abstract: we investigate the structure of interior electromagnetic fields compatible with the exterior kerr-newman geometry when regular interior geometries for describing regular black hole solutions are considered. working within the gürses-gürsey framework and considering a rotating de sitter-type geometry in the interior region, we analyze a particular class of electromagnetic fields aligned with the principal null directions and satisfying maxwell electrodynamics. we show that, within such a class of interior electromagnetic fields, no well-behaved interior electromagnetic field can be supported in the absence of electromagnetic currents. moreover, we show that for the same interior and exterior geometries, different types of interior electromagnetic fields and charge distributions, together with different charge densities on the rotating boundary shell, can be constructed while matching the same exterior kerr-newman electromagnetic field. this results highlight the non-uniqueness of the interior electromagnetic structure compatible with a given kerr-newman exterior. for a particular choice of interior electromagnetic fields we show that the de sitter fluid can be interpreted as being electrically polarized by the rotating charged shell. in this case, the interior region contains no net electric charge, which is instead concentrated entirely on the shell, and the interior medium behaves as a perfect conductor with infinite conductivity. in a second choice for the electromagnetic field, we show that the polarized de sitter fluid also contributes to the total electric charge, with the interior medium acting as a nonisotropic conductor.

title: cosmological pole-skipping, shock waves and quantum chaotic dynamics of de sitter horizons
abstract: we present a systematic analysis of pole-skipping for scalar, maxwell, and gravitational waves in cosmological spacetimes. specifically, working in empty de sitter space and in schwarzschild-de sitter black hole geometries, we locate the tower of pole-skipping points of such fields and show that they impose nontrivial constraints on the corresponding bulk two-point functions. focusing on the gravitational sound channel, we then extract the lyapunov exponent and butterfly velocities that characterize hypothetical dual many-body quantum chaos at each horizon. these chaotic data precisely match the outcome of a gravitational shock wave calculation, confirming that the relevant pole-skipping points encode high-energy scattering of horizon quanta. interestingly, the butterfly velocities can become superluminal or imaginary, with the latter signaling a spatially modulated propagation of chaos. assuming that a holographic dual exists, we translate our results into field theory language and propose that the dual theory can be divided into two entangled sectors that capture the black hole and cosmological horizon degrees of freedom. our results suggest that the black hole sector becomes increasingly nonlocal as the black hole shrinks and that the cosmological horizon sector exhibits behavior compatible with violations of hermiticity. finally, we outline simple microscopic toy models, built from long-range and non-hermitian deformations of the double scaled sachdev-ye-kitaev (dssyk)-type chains, that realize these features, providing a concrete arena for future exploration.

title: probing compact binary coalescences in the decihertz gw band with indigo-d
abstract: we present an astrophysical science-case study of indigo-d, a decihertz gravitational-wave mission concept, focusing on compact binary sources across the 0.1-10 hz band bridging lisa and next-generation ground-based interferometers. for these science projections, we consider three spacecraft forming an l-shaped interferometer in a heliocentric orbit, with two orthogonal 1000 km arms sharing a common vertex. we calculate the time-dependent antenna response of this geometry, including modulation produced by the orbital motion of the constellation. we treat the strain-sensitivity curve supplied by the indigo-d collaboration as an input. for the assumed sensitivity, we estimate a bns detection rate of $\sim76$-$767\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$.   we compute horizon distances for different source classes and find that intermediate-mass black-hole binaries with masses $10^2$-$10^3\,m_\odot$ are detectable throughout their formation history, complementing the reach of lisa and terrestrial detectors. binary neutron star systems are observable to a horizon redshift of $z\lesssim0.3$, allowing continuous multi-band coverage with voyager-class interferometers from the decihertz regime to merger. a bayesian parameter-estimation study of a gw170817-like binary shows that the sky localization area improves from $\sim21\,{\rm deg}^2$ at one month, $\sim1\,{\rm deg}^2$ at one week, down to $0.3\,{\rm deg}^2$ at six hours pre-merger. these sky areas are readily tiled by the rubin observatory, whose $9.6\,{\rm deg}^2$ field of view and r-band depth enable high-cadence, repeated coverage of gw170817-like kilonovae at this distance and beyond. indigo-d bridges the gap between millihertz and terrestrial observations, enabling early warnings on timescales from months to hours and enhancing the prospects for multi-band and multi-messenger discoveries. (abridged)

title: shadow of rotating black hole surrounded by dark matter
abstract: dark matter (dm), a fundamental cosmic component, motivates the study of its influence on black hole (bh) shadows, especially for spinning bhs confirmed by eht observations. this work generalizes the schwarzschild bh surrounded by dm to an axisymmetric kerr bh using the newman-janis algorithm (nja), investigating the resulting event horizon and ergosphere structures. employing null geodesics, we examine the effects of dm mass $δm$ on bh shadow, including its radius, distortion, and the associated energy emission rate. our analysis reveals that dm has a negligible effect below a critical mass, once this threshold is surpassed, all bh structures expand significantly. furthermore, dm robustly contributes to the shadow maintaining a near circular shape, even for highly spinning bhs. this pronounced structural expansion under high dm mass may potentially exceed current observational constraints, suggesting that dm must either be absent in the immediate vicinity of the bh or its localized mass must remain below this critical value to be consistent with astrophysical observations.

title: quantum gravitational contrast in creating schrödinger cat state
abstract: in this paper, we illustrate how a schrödinger cat state created via a matter-wave interferometer can be viewed as the simplest quantum-gravity setup where we can treat both matter and gravity on an equal footing at a perturbative level. here we treat einstein's theory of general relativity using an effective field theory approach, quantising the massless spin-2 graviton in the presence of a quantum spatial superposition of matter that creates a matter-wave interferometer in the non-relativistic limit. we show that, due to the matter-graviton coupling, the graviton vacuum is displaced analogous to the coherent state. we study the contrast/overlap between the coherent states of the left and right superpositions in the matter-wave interferometer. we also study the entanglement between matter and the graviton in this setup and relate it to a gravitational contrast, or the overlap of the quantum geometries led by the coherent states. in the appendix, we provide an example of a time-dependent harmonic oscillator and study the contrast/overlap of such coherent states of the graviton.

title: demagnetizing kbr and new ricci-flat rotating metric
abstract: we construct a new ricci-flat metric by demagnetizing the recently reported kerr-bertotti-robinson (kbr) solution. the metric is a deformation of the kerr metric characterized by a parameter $b$, so that the asymptotic kerr becomes a regular dome of spindle shape with north and south poles. despite lacking an asymptotically-flat region, we find that the first law of black hole thermodynamics can be established. some thermodynamic relations are identical to those of the kerr black hole, as if the constant $b$ is absent. our ricci-flat rotating metric serves a neutral seed for a variety of inequivalent schemes of magnetizing the schwarzschild and kerr black holes.

title: global curvature control in a regular black hole with minkowski core and inner-extremal horizon
abstract: we construct a static, spherically symmetric regular black hole with a minkowski core, a non-extremal outer horizon, and a degenerate inner horizon with vanishing surface gravity. the spacetime exhibits two main features. first, in the large-mass regime with $r_+=2m$, the maximal kretschmann scalar becomes nearly independent of the adm mass and is mainly controlled by the inner-horizon radius $r_-$, providing a simple sufficient condition for the curvature to remain sub-planckian everywhere. second, the effective cubic zero of the metric function replaces the standard exponential near-horizon amplification with power-law behavior. a massless scalar test field shows that the geometric blueshift factor grows as $v^{3/2}$. then, we use the double-null shell and ori models to examine the corresponding effective mass dynamics. the nonlinear shell-crossing contribution decays at late times, while the ori evolution with a price-law ingoing flux keeps the internal misner-sharp mass bounded. in both descriptions, the late-time mass approaches $r_-/2$. the same inner-horizon scale therefore controls the global curvature bound and the finite mass scale reached by the shell dynamics.

title: gravitational wave propagation in k-essence cosmology: theory and observational constraints
abstract: gravitational waves (gws) provide a powerful, theory-independent probe of the dynamical structure of spacetime and the cosmological background. we investigate the propagation of linearized tensor modes in k-essence cosmology, where the dark sector is described by a non-canonical scalar field. working in the high-frequency (short-wavelength) limit on a friedmann-lema\^ıtre-robertson-walker background and restricting to the transverse-traceless sector, we obtain a modified evolution equation in which the gw speed remains strictly luminal (compatible with gw170817), while the background field $\barϕ$ generates a time-dependent effective mass term $m_{\rm eff}$. this background-induced mass alters the dispersion relation without introducing extra propagating degrees of freedom, producing an accumulated, frequency-dependent phase shift over cosmological distances. we show that $m_{\rm eff}$ is uniquely determined by background cosmological parameters and can be expressed as a redshift-dependent function $m_{\rm eff}(z)$, providing a direct connection between gw observables and scalar-field dynamics. the gw luminosity distance stays identical to the electromagnetic one, preserving standard-siren consistency. we confront the model with a joint bayesian analysis combining cosmic chronometers, bao, pantheon+sh0es, and standard-siren measurements from gwtc-2.1/3/4, and assess performance using $χ^2$, $χ^2_{\rm red}$, aic, bic, and dic. the reconstruction is consistent with current data, reproduces the late-time expansion history, and provides data-driven constraints on the redshift evolution of $m_{\rm eff}(z)$.

title: intermediate states in chaotic triple evolution and applications to black hole merger statistics
abstract: three-body interactions exhibit phases of strong chaotic evolution as well as hierarchical motion where one body separates from a binary and follows a hyperbolic or elliptic trajectory around it. the binaries produced during phases of hierarchical motion may lead to gravitational wave (gw) inspirals, but this depends on the outcomes of the chaotic states. in this paper we re-derive the elliptic outcome distribution using equilibrium statistical mechanics and explore it together with the hyperbolic distribution. when comparing to n-body simulations, we find that we can reduce the elliptic outcome model to one free parameter instead of the previously used two and that the predicted disintegration probabilities agree except for very low angular momentum triples. we then use both outcome distributions along with a star cluster model to design a monte carlo algorithm for repeated binary-single scatterings within dense star systems. we explore star cluster masses of $[10^5 - 10^7] m_{\odot}$, with the goal of quantifying observably eccentric merger (oem) gws, visible to instruments such as ligo and virgo. assuming an oem detection sensitivity of $f_{\rm min}=10 {\rm hz}, e_{\rm min} = 0.1$, we find the elliptic oems are about $\sim (32 - 63)\%$ of the total elliptic mergers and that the total cluster mass greatly impacts the fraction of ejected binaries. the oem to total merger fraction (oem fraction) is found to be $(2.6 - 4.4)\%$. considering the detection sensitivity that gw interferometers have today $(f_{\rm min} \simeq 34.4 {\rm hz})$ we obtain the oem fraction in the $(1.6 - 3.1)\%$ range.

title: searching for extra dimensions with gravitational waves: dark-siren constraints from gwtc-4
abstract: higher-dimensional theories of gravity predict that gravitational waves (gws) can propagate into extra spatial dimensions, leading to modified amplitude damping over cosmological distances. measurements of gw luminosity distances therefore provide a unique probe of the dimensionality of spacetime. in this work, we constrain higher-dimensional gw propagation using the dark-siren method with the gravitational-wave transient catalog 4.0 (gwtc-4). we adopt a phenomenological parameterization motivated by braneworld scenarios, in which deviations from general relativity are characterized by the spacetime dimension number $d$ and a crossover scale $r_c$ governing the transition between four- and higher-dimensional gravity. we perform a hierarchical bayesian analysis combining 141 compact binary coalescences from gwtc-4 with line-of-sight galaxy information from the glade+ catalog. for a prior $h_0 \in [65,77]\ {\rm km~s^{-1}mpc^{-1}}$ and $\log(r_c/{\rm mpc}) \in [2.7,4.0]$, we obtain $d = 4.38^{+1.91}_{-1.01}$ (68\% credible interval). we also find that the inferred posterior distribution of $r_c$ accumulates near the upper prior boundary, indicating that the crossover scale remains poorly constrained by current observations. we further show that the inferred constraint on $d$ depends sensitively on the assumed prior range of $r_c$, which determines the characteristic distance scale at which deviations from general relativity become significant. our results provide the first gwtc-4 dark-siren constraints on higher-dimensional gw propagation and demonstrate that current observations remain consistent with four-dimensional general relativity.

title: regular black holes from anisotropic source with hydrodynamic equation of state
abstract: we study regular black hole solutions sourced by an anisotropic energy momentum tensor. it is well known that the geometry of the interior of a spherically symmetric regular black hole approaches the ds metric. having decomposed the energy momentum tensor into its isotropic and anisotropic components, we assume a hydrodynamic equation of state, $p= p(ρ)$, for the pressure, and look for spherically symmetric, regular black hole solutions. we consider different forms of $ p(ρ)$ which yield the previously known regular black hole solutions, as well as various new metrics. we show that the profile of $ p(ρ)$ has a root and a maximum as it approaches $0^+$ at large distances. consequently, the square of the sound speed of perturbations, $c_s^2$, changes sign at the point where $p$ reaches its maximum, indicating a potential hydrodynamic instability. in addition, imposing the subluminal bound on $c_s$ puts strong constraints on the model parameters, excluding models in which the energy density has an exponential fall off. we establish a universal hierarchy among the relative positions at which the strong energy condition is violated, at which $p$ has its root, and at which $p$ attains its maximum.

title: quasinormal modes as probes of black hole reentrant phase transitions
abstract: we investigate the interplay between thermodynamic phase transitions and the dynamical behavior of quasi-normal modes (qnms) in weakly nonlinear charged anti-de sitter black holes. in a non-extended phase space, we identify a reentrant large-small-large(intermediate) phase transition for these black holes. employing the shooting method to solve the klein-gordon equation for a massless scalar field, we compute qnm frequencies across these phases, revealing distinct behaviors in different phases. specifically, to our knowledge, this is the first report of utilizing qnms as dynamical probes of thermodynamic phases during reentrant phase transitions including zeroth and first-order transitions. these findings establish qnms as a powerful dynamical probe for thermodynamic phase transitions, providing new insights into the thermodynamic and dynamical properties of nonlinear charged black holes as well.

title: learning effective bulk fields from fermionic spectra: application to an extended power-law liquid model for cuprate strange metals
abstract: we develop a neural-ode framework to infer effective bulk metric functions and the charge-weighted gauge potential from boundary fermionic spectra within a static, planar black-hole ansatz. controlled benchmarks recover the known bulk profiles of the einstein--maxwell and gubser--rocha models. we then use normalized interaction self-energy targets generated from an extended power-law liquid model with parameters calibrated by angle-resolved photoemission measurements to test the proposed geometric explanation of cuprate strange-metal spectra in a semi-holographic setting. for this application, we use a massless probe in backgrounds with conformal-to-$\mathrm{ads}_2\times\mathbb{r}^2$ asymptotics and derive a spectral extraction formula from the conserved radial dirac flux. we identify coordinate/weyl redundancy and a degeneracy in the scaled hawking temperature of the normalized inverse problem. the conformal factor remains undetermined, so bulk entropy and the associated contribution to electronic specific heat require independent input. low-temperature targets are fitted accurately across the studied doping range. in the high-temperature test, however, the present ansatz and optimization search have not yielded a refined geometry that accurately reproduces the thermal spectral shape while preserving frequency symmetry. these results may guide the further development of semi-holographic models for cuprates, and the framework may also find applications in other strongly correlated electron systems.

title: quasi-bound states and late-time evolution of a massive fermion around a reissner-nordström black hole
abstract: a massive fermion around a charged black hole provides a gravitational analogue of atomic bound states and their relaxation. in this work, we study this system by formulating the radial equation as a coupled matrix system and constructing the green's function with ingoing boundary conditions at the horizon and decaying boundary conditions at infinity. in the weak-coupling scenario $|qq|\sim mm<1$, a matrix matching scheme gives an improved analytic expression of quasi-bound-state spectrum, including fine-structure corrections and more accurate decay widths. the extremal reissner-nordström case ($|q|=m$) is treated separately and shown to be the smooth limiting result of the non-extremal spectrum. we further analyze the branch-cut contribution to the time-domain green's function in the late-time limit. we confirm an oscillatory power-law behavior in intermediate late-time regime $1/m < t < 1/m^3m^2$. in the far late-time regime $t>1/m^3m^2$, the activation of the quasi-bound states produces an $t^{-5/6}\exp(-ηt^{1/3})$ suppression with a chirping phase before the asymptotic $t^{-5/6}$ tail previously found in the limit $t\to\infty$. direct time-domain simulations support this distinction and show how the quasi-bound contribution coexists with the familiar power-law component.

title: spin-mediated modulation of chaos bound violation in lorentz-violating black hole spacetimes
abstract: in this paper, we investigate how the particle spin modulates chaos bound violations in lorentz-violating black hole spacetimes within the framework of bumblebee gravity. using the mathisson-papapetrou-dixon formalism, we analyze the effects of spin-curvature coupling, lorentz symmetry breaking, and the cosmological constant on the orbital instability in static spherically symmetric (a)ds black holes. we find that the particle spin provides an additional mechanism for modulating the critical angular momentum associated with the onset of violation. the lorentz-violating parameter suppresses the violations by reducing the accessible parameter space and the critical charge. meanwhile, a negative cosmological constant decreases the violation region but enhances the violation magnitude for allowed configurations. our results demonstrate that the spin and lorentz symmetry breaking jointly regulate the interplay between orbital instability and black hole horizon properties.

title: probing an intermediate-mass black hole companion of sagittarius a* with pulsar timing
abstract: an intermediate-mass black hole (imbh) hidden in our galactic center (gc) may explain the puzzling observations of the stellar distribution around sagittarius a* (sgr a*), the supermassive black hole (smbh) in the gc. future observations with the next-generation radio telescopes, such as the ska, are promising to discover pulsars orbiting around sgr a*, and thus provide the possibility of constraining the hidden imbh with pulsar timing. we study the detectability of a third-body, the imbh, in the pulsar-smbh system based on radio timing observation. we find that the pulsar-smbh system is very sensitive to such a third-body perturbation and can be used to put stringent constraints on the existence of the imbh. even under strong perturbations caused by the complex gc astrophysical environments, timing observation will still complement the existing observational constraints.

title: spin-inversion degeneracies in restricted inspiral waveforms for lisa
abstract: spin inversions appear in several settings. analytical work predicts a single spin flip during unequal-mass supermassive binary inspiral, while numerical relativity and post-newtonian calculations show repeated flip-flop motion in comparable-mass binaries. secular spin evolution also predicts additional cases driven by spin-induced mass quadrupoles. whether these effects can be distinguished in gravitational-wave data is still unclear. we combine the secular spin angle equations with a quasi-circular second post-newtonian frequency evolution and build a restricted waveform weighted by the sky-averaged lisa sensitivity. we study five near-equal-mass injections with detector-frame total mass $m=2\times10^5m_\odot$, including kerr flip-flops and one quadrupole-induced case. each injection is compared with physically evolving waveforms constrained to have no orbital-plane crossings. we search all four no-inversion sectors, vary the masses, spin magnitudes, and initial spin angles, and maximize over time, phase, and overall amplitude. large spin motion does not by itself lead to a clearly different waveform in this restricted model. we compare configurations with different spin magnitudes, relative spin orientations, and angular excursions at eleven observer inclinations between $0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. with each injection normalized to signal snr $ρ_\star=100$, four of the five cases leave a residual snr below unity for the $0^\circ$ viewing direction along the total angular momentum. at nonzero inclinations, the residual associated with the largest match found reaches $7.07$ in the two-active-spin case at $55^\circ$. these upper bounds on the minimum residual within the allowed template family suggest potential distinguishability of spin inversions and motivate studies with more complete waveforms and the full lisa response.

title: joule thomson expansion of $κ$-deformed schwarzschild-ads black hole
abstract: we investigate the joule-thomson expansion of a non-commutative schwarzschild-ads black hole, whose space-time geometry is described by the lie-algebraic $κ$-deformed space-time, and show that the $κ$-deformation parameter induces joule-thomson expansion in an uncharged-ads black hole. we find the ratio of minimum inversion temperature to critical temperature $t_i^{(min)}/t_c \simeq 0.493$, is independent of the deformation parameter, and is in close agreement with the value for reissner-nordstrom black hole. furthermore, we show the existence of a minimum black hole mass (depending on the $κ$-deformation parameter) below which the joule-thomson expansion vanishes.

title: screened scalar hair and the weak-lensing separation of black holes from neutron stars in quadratic $f(r)$ gravity
abstract: quadratic $f(r)$ gravity carries a massive scalar degree of freedom, the scalaron, whose finite range $λ$ screens its influence on the geometry outside a compact object. we show that this screening severs the exterior of a black hole from that of a neutron star of the same mass. correction to the schwarzschild metric is yukawa-suppressed, falling as $e^{-r/λ}$ in the coupling, and is thus invisible to any expansion in powers of that coupling; the exterior is moreover intrinsically isotropic, so that inverting the temporal potential alone, as one does for single-potential solutions, fails to solve the field equations. applying the gibbons & werner method of the gauss-bonnet theorem to this geometry, we find the leading deflection angle to be exactly the general-relativistic, ($b$: impact parameter), scalaron contributions cancelling identically in the combination that bends light. first correction carries the unfamiliar signature $λ^{-1/2}b^{-3/2}e^{-b/λ}$, screened beyond the scalaron range and confirmed against direct quadrature to around 20% at $b=4λ$, improving to 7% at $b=12λ$. what survives is the ingredients that deliver it, namely, non-analyticity in the coupling, the intrinsically isotropic gauge, the closed-form screened correction and the pressure-weighted scalar charge, are obtained within a single, self-consistent derivation here. a static black hole carries no scalar hair, and lenses precisely as general relativity requires; a neutron star acquires a scalar charge weighted by the pressure supporting it against collapse, and does not. weak lensing therefore closes as a discriminant of the theory, whilst the horizon, as against a material surface, remains one in principle. the observational advantage lies in the strong-field imaging of the photon sphere, and in the stellar interior, where the scalar charge is fixed by the equation of state.

title: static tidal love numbers of schwarzschild and non-schwarzschild black holes in quadratic gravity
abstract: we calculate the static electric quadrupolar response of black holes in four-dimensional quadratic gravity, with action $r-αc^2+βr^2$. the schwarzschild solution has zero massless gravitational love number under the stated boundary conditions. a numerical non-schwarzschild solution instead has a nonzero negative response. at $α/r_h^2=1/2$, we find $λ_e/r_h^5\simeq-0.1224928$ and $k_2^{(r_h)}\simeq-0.1837391$, with a final outer-endpoint change in $k_2^{(r_h)}$ of about $1.60\times10^{-7}$. we explain how the background is obtained by shooting and how the tidal solution is selected by matching at an intermediate radius. the perturbations are written in kodama--ishibashi gauge-invariant variables. after the scalar-curvature perturbation is excluded by horizon regularity and the absence of an applied scalar tide, the remaining static sector has three coupled second-order radial equations. we define the curvature amplitudes in these equations and describe why simple attempts to separate them fail. the coupling scan shows a negative response approaching zero near the schwarzschild intersection. we also explain why this full-theory result does not conflict with the removal of curvature-squared operators in a perturbative low-energy expansion.

title: radius of the innermost stable circular orbit of black-holes with localized astrophysical dark matter halo
abstract: we investigate the geodesic structure of a static, spherically symmetric black-hole in the   background of a localized astrophysical dark matter (adm)-halo. the halo is modeled by a   core-radius ($r_0$), regularized density profile that vanishes at the event horizon   and exponential factor ensures the finite total halo mass. we solved the einstein field   equations numerically with equation of state with $p=wρ$ for stiff matter $w=1$ scenario.   by analyzing the effective potential and its first and second derivatives, we evaluated the   characteristic radius of the time-like innermost stable circular orbit ($r_{\text{isco}}$)   of massive particle in the vicinity of hairy black-hole. our numerical analysis is consistent   with the recently proposed theoretical upper bound $r_{\text{isco}} \le 6$ normalized to   unit mass black-hole. we showed that the adm-halo shifts $r_{\text{isco}}$ inward with respect   to the schwarzschild (bald) scenario and the shifts are larger for larger halo core-radius.   in particular our numerical finding enumerate $r_{\text{isco}}$ are approximately   $5.97$, $5.61$, $5.53$ for $r_0=2.0,10.0,20.0$ respectively. we believe that our analysis   with adm-halo model shed light on probing black-hole hair through high-energy   astrophysical observables.

title: complexification of the kerr-ads black hole thermodynamic phase transition
abstract: in this paper, we establish a systematic complex-analytical framework for investigating the thermodynamics of high-dimensional singly spinning kerr-ads black holes. by performing an analytical continuation of the black hole horizon radius into the complex plane, we map the thermodynamic behavior for the black hole to the zeros distribution of the corresponding analytical function. in the region below the critical point, this approach provides the criterion for identifying phase transitions and reveals that the zeroth-order phase transition does not alter the underlying thermodynamic topological structure of the black hole. in the supercritical region, based on the lee-yang theory of phase transition, we construct the widom line to characterize the supercritical crossover behavior for the kerr-ads black holes. this study provides a new perspective on the thermodynamic analysis of black holes.

title: weak cosmic censorship in einstein-born-infeld black hole: a parameter-space analysis
abstract: einstein-born-infeld is a charged black hole solution of general relativity with born-infeld nonlinear electrodynamics, which has interesting physical features. it violates bekenstein's entropy upper bound, and it can overcharge with respect to the reissner-nordström black hole. it presents an optimum situation to test the cosmic censorship conjecture, which is another important conjecture in black hole physics. in principle, this analysis requires the calculation of the self-energy of a test particle in the vicinity of the black hole, which, in general, is not feasible because of the electromagnetic nonlinearities. in this work, we propose an alternative approach that allows us to explore the whole parameter space of the einstein-born-infeld black hole and test the validity of the cosmic censorship conjecture.

title: scalar fields in the background of a linear vaidya spacetime
abstract: we study, in a semiclassical, quasi-stationary approximation, the entanglement properties of massless scalar fields near the event horizon of a dynamical black hole modeled by an ingoing vaidya metric with a linearly decaying mass. in the near-horizon limit, the geometry becomes conformally equivalent to an eternal black hole, allowing the use of modular theory to analyze vacuum entanglement. we first study the modifications to the entanglement across the bifurcation surface of such a black hole from that of an eternal one. the conformal factor accounting for the evaporation modifies the bogoliubov transformation, inducing a phase in the thermofield-double-like structure of the global vacuum. this phase change of the vacuum state is a consequence of the adiabatic shift of the horizon. a quantitative measure of the entanglement change due to the phase is obtained through the clauser-horne-shimony-holt (chsh) inequality. we compare the chsh inequalities in the vacuum states for the static and the linear vaidya black holes and find that the chsh correlation quantity for the latter is decreased by a factor depending on the evaporation rate.   next, we discuss the changes that must be considered for the linear vaidya black hole formed from gravitational collapse. for this purpose we adapt an analysis by wald for the case of the schwarzschild black hole. we find, as expected, the near-horizon structure and state do not approach that of the eternal black hole. rather, the thermal factor is modified by a factor incorporating the change in the black hole mass due to evaporation. the entangled global vacuum state again has a thermofield double structure with the modification mentioned above.

title: complex spinodals and supercritical crossovers in kerr-newman-ads$_4$ black holes
abstract: we study supercritical crossovers in four-dimensional kerr-newman-ads black holes at fixed angular momentum and charge. from the exact enthalpy, we prove uniqueness of the physical critical point and positivity of the quartic landau coefficient throughout the charge-rotation family, treating the uncharged kerr-ads endpoint in separate scaling variables. an exact quartic reduction determines the coexistence entropies and latent heat throughout the subcritical regime. above criticality, the two physical spinodals continue as a complex conjugate pair. their real temperature projection defines a widom-type line, and varying the charge-rotation ratio assembles these lines into a crossover surface. the landau cusp fixes the imaginary entropy and temperature to scale with the square root and three-halves powers of the pressure displacement from criticality. the projected fold and the local heat capacity ridge share a critical tangent. we derive their leading quadratic temperature separation and prove that the ridge lies at a higher temperature near criticality. exact endpoint solutions and numerical continuation check these predictions. the cusp exponents are common to the family, while the crossover temperature depends on the thermodynamic criterion used to define it.

title: bayesian inference of primary hair from black hole shadows in generalized proca theory
abstract: we investigate black hole shadows and observational constraints on primary vector hair in an exact rotating solution of generalized proca theory. selecting a coupling slice yields a simple, one-parameter kerr deformation that is noncircular and depends on spin and latitude. the deformation vanishes in the nonrotating limit, while the vector field remains nontrivial. we determine the domain admitting a regular outer horizon and construct shadow and lensing images by numerical ray tracing. ray-traced images show a modest enlargement of the shadow and changes in the surrounding lensing pattern. bayesian inference using the shadow area-equivalent radius and axis ratio yields joint constraints on hair, spin, and viewing inclination from event horizon telescope observations of m87* and sgr a*. the m87* posterior favors relatively low spin and exhibits a pronounced spin--hair anticorrelation, while sgr a* yields upper limits on spin and hair with its inclination remaining essentially unconstrained. these results connect the optical signatures of primary vector hair to quantitative horizon-scale constraints.

title: critical limits of accelerating kerr--nut spacetimes and the non-expanding plebański--demiański family
abstract: we study degenerate-horizon limits of vacuum accelerating kerr--nut spacetimes with finite, nonzero nut parameter. at cubic criticality, $a^2=m^2+\ell^2$ and $αm=1$, a projective coordinate transformation relates the complete critical parent metrics by a local homothety. the cubic horizon has one finite axis and a noncompact angular end, and its near-horizon limit is locally homothetic to the swirling universe. explicit four-dimensional coordinate transformations place the ordinary extremal, nariai and cubic near-horizon metrics in the negative-, positive- and zero-curvature longitudinal sectors of the non-expanding plebański--demiański family. the nariai correspondence includes an exceptional endpoint that requires a separate killing chart. under a cubic-adapted near-critical scaling, fixed first-order separations between the approaching horizons do not affect the leading metric. the global killing identifications and regular completion of the critical parent remain open.

title: destinies of plasmoids formed from the magnetic reconnection occurring within the ergo region of a rotating black hole
abstract: it is widely accepted that magnetic reconnections occur successively in black hole accretion flows, especially on the equatorial plane, owing to the formation of the equatorial current sheet. when magnetic reconnection takes place within the ergosphere of a rotating black hole, one of the ejected plasmoids (denoted as $p_-$) may acquire negative energy-at-infinity density, while the companion plasmoid (denoted as $p_+$) correspondingly carries the energy extracted from the black hole. this mechanism, known as the comisso-asenjo process, provides a viable astrophysical pathway for extracting energy from a rotating black hole. generally speaking, two conditions have to be satisfied for successful energy extraction. first, $p_-$ is generated via magnetic reconnection with negative energy-at-infinity density. second, the associated $p_+$, which carries the extracted energy, must escape to infinity. though a number of studies have promoted the theory of the comisso-asenjo process, the escape of $p_+$ lacks consideration. in this work, we adopt geodesic approach to systematically examine the destinies of $p_+$ after ejection, thereby establishing the complete conditions for energy extraction from a rotating black hole via magnetic reconnection. we redefine the covering factor, for which only escaping $p_+$ are counted. this quantity reflects how probable the successful energy extraction occurs in an accretion system. through analysis of this revised covering factor, we identify a lower bound on the black hole spin, $a=0.8005$, below which energy extraction via magnetic reconnection can never succeed, no matter how high the magnetization of the bulk plasma is. this limit suggests that the spin-down of a black hole caused by successive magnetic reconnections would terminate once the spin decreases to approximately 0.8005.

title: a new regime of the c-metric: super accelerating black holes
abstract: we define and investigate the super accelerating regime of the charged c-metric, which arises at large acceleration. in this regime, the polar coordinate must be restricted to a smaller interval within $(0,π)$, and the resulting boundary defines a new axis of symmetry. this changes the conical singularity structure of the spacetime and, consequently, its string/strut interpretation. we further show that, when the conical defect at the south pole is removed, the komar mass takes the simple form $m_k=1/(4a)$, up to the normalization of the time translation killing vector. finally, we explore the near extremal limits of this regime, identifying new limiting geometries.

title: moving beyond quasinormal modes and reinterpreting direct waves in binary black hole merger-ringdowns
abstract: based on black-hole perturbation-theory calculations and an effective-one-body picture of binary black hole mergers, it has been suggested that a direct wave may be present and measurable in the ringdown. furthermore, it has been suggested that this signal might originate from substantially inside the light ring (or photon sphere) of the remnant black hole, perhaps even from close to the event horizon. in this paper, we present three independent strands of evidence against such claims. in the process, we show that there is indeed an early-time part of the ringdown signal that cannot be directly modeled by quasinormal modes. however, there is no evidence that this is a direct wave as it has previously been defined, and we show that the properties of this component are related to the remnant's light ring rather than its horizon.

title: probing parity-breaking black-hole geometry with extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
abstract: we investigate the gravitational-wave signatures of equatorial reflection symmetry breaking in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (emris) around a parity-violating conformal kerr black hole. for the circular-orbit branch connected to equatorial kerr orbits, we derive the dynamics through second order in the dimensionless deformation parameter $\varepsilon$ and construct adiabatic inspirals and gravitational-wave signals using a mass-quadrupole prescription. equatorial reflection maps $\varepsilon$ to $-\varepsilon$, making the polar displacement odd and the orbital frequency and energy even in the deformation. the induced first harmonic has a small direct contribution for the configurations studied, while second-order dynamical corrections accumulate over many cycles to produce appreciable dephasing. we find that rapid black-hole rotation enhances these phase effects and the associated noise-weighted waveform mismatch. for a one-year inspiral of a $10m_\odot$ object into a $10^6m_\odot$ black hole with $a/m=0.9$ and viewing inclination $ι=2π/3$, the fixed-parameter mismatch reaches the comparison benchmark $\mathcal m=0.01$ at approximately $\varepsilon=10^{-3}$, without optimization over time, phase, or kerr parameters. a single-parameter fisher analysis also indicates improved local sensitivity to $\varepsilon$ at high spin. these results connect the reflection properties of the circular branch to accumulated source-phase effects and complement tests of propagation birefringence. the sensitivity estimates remain conditional on the adiabatic quadrupole model and the adopted comparison procedure; robust observational constraints require more accurate radiation modeling and a full parameter-estimation analysis.

title: scattering of scalar waves by scalarized black holes in einstein-scalar-gauss-bonnet gravity
abstract: we systematically investigate the scattering and absorption of a massive scalar field by scalarized black holes in einstein-scalar-gauss-bonnet gravity with quartic coupling $f(ϕ)=α(ϕ^{2}+βϕ^{4})$ and exponential coupling $f(ϕ)=α(1-\operatorname{e}^{-βϕ^{2}})$. the background solutions are obtained numerically via a chebyshev pseudospectral method, enabling a partial-wave analysis on purely numerical black hole backgrounds. the partial-wave results are cross-validated against geodesic and glory approximations and the schwarzschild limit with excellent agreements. we find that scalarization suppresses the total absorption cross section relative to the schwarzschild case, and produces distinctive signatures in the differential scattering cross section. a qualitative difference between the two coupling models is identified: for the quartic coupling model, deviations from schwarzschild are concentrated in the intermediate-angle region $\sim(70^{\circ},140^{\circ})$, with comparatively small changes at forward angles and near the glory peak; for the exponential coupling model, deviations appear across the full angular range and substantially modify the glory peak, which in some parameter regimes can even exceed the schwarzschild value. this distinctive angular pattern provides a potential diagnostic for distinguishing esgb coupling functions from scattering observables.

title: the geometry of the "gauge argument"
abstract: we show how the "gauge argument", widely criticized by philosophers as ad hoc and unconvincing, may be reconstructed rigorously, and, we believe, convincingly, as an argument concerning the geometry of vector bundles. in this form, the gauge argument has two parts, the first of which is strongly analogous to the weyl-stein argument for galilean spacetime as the appropriate setting for newtonian gravitation; and the second of which invokes a classic result in the yang-mills theory literature, due to utiyama [1956, "invariant theoretical interpretation of interaction", phys. rev. 101, 1597].

title: black hole free energy landscapes from constrained instantons
abstract: we apply gravitational path integral factorization to provide a semiclassical interpretation of generalized black hole free energy landscapes at fixed external temperature and angular velocities. boundary integral transforms express the formal partition function as an integral over constrained sectors labeled by complete local partial-neumann data on an auxiliary hypersurface. independent variation establishes paired regular subregion solutions as constrained instantons, with lagrange multipliers supporting lapse and tangential shift jumps that accommodate thermal and rotational mismatches. for selected nonextremal stationary families with an asymptotic boundary, the constrained saddle action takes the form $i_{\rm constr}=β\mathcal f_{\rm gen}=β(e_{\mathcal b}-ω_{\mathcal b}^{i}j_{\mathcal b,i})-s$, with $β=t^{-1}$. here $e_{\mathcal b}$ and $j_{\mathcal b,i}$ are renormalized hamiltonian charges and $s$ is the black hole entropy, whose contribution to the action comes from the regular horizon cap. interior stationary points of the landscape correspond to smooth equilibrium saddles when the retained variations independently span the entropy and angular momentum directions. we extend the construction to local, parity-even $f(\mathrm{riemann})$ theories without curvature derivatives by retaining the complete auxiliary interface data. the same thermodynamic form follows with wald entropy, without a small-deficit expansion. schwarzschild and kerr black holes illustrate the einstein construction, while five-dimensional static ads black holes in einstein--gauss--bonnet gravity and the rotating btz branch of new massive gravity provide explicit checks of the higher-curvature extension.

title: periodic orbits and gravitational-wave emission from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals around rotating charged black holes in nonlinear electrodynamics
abstract: within general-relativistic descriptions, the no-hair theorem dictates that black-hole geometries possess just three intrinsic physical quantities: mass, angular momentum, and electric charge. black holes in nonlinear electrodynamics (ned) are equivalent to those composed of anisotropic matter and can develop "hair" structures near the event horizon, serving as ideal testbeds for modified theories of gravity. working within einsteinian gravitational theory, we adopt a coupling construction between gravity and ned matter, focusing explicitly on the einstein-euler-heisenberg (eeh) variant with the power-index parameter fixed at s = 2. in this framework, a rotating, charged ned black hole extends the kerr-newman geometry with extra correction terms. treating spin a and ned charge q as primary control variables, we examine test-particle dynamics inside extreme-mass-ratio inspiral (emri) configurations. we derive equatorial timelike geodesics and the effective potential. through numerical evaluation of marginally-bound orbits (mbo) and innermost stable circular orbits (isco), we explore how these parameters reshape the energy-angular-momentum (e-l) phase-space. using the (z, w, v) integer-valued orbit taxonomy, we compute the two gravitational-wave polarization modes h+ and hx via the adiabatic approximation and quadrupole radiation prescription. larger values for a and q drive inward contraction for bound trajectories while displacing the e-l phase-space toward smaller angular-momentum values. periodic-orbit zoom-whirl signatures grow increasingly prominent, while larger parameter values shorten the waveform periods and enhance signal amplitudes. our results provide theoretical support for space-borne gravitational-wave observatories including lisa and tianqin, enabling prospects for discriminating ned black-hole spacetimes and performing observational checks on the no-hair theorem.

title: local scale symmetry and black holes
abstract: we derive solutions for a black hole coupled to a real scalar field under considerations of local scale symmetry. starting with the simple case $(λ=0)$, we find the solutions and derive the black hole's temperature, entropy, and its effective mass, and observe an adiabatic accretion of the scalar field onto the black hole. as a result, the effective mass of the black hole grows. in the general case $(λ\ne 0)$, the situation becomes more intricate; the horizons (the vanishing points of $g_{tt}$) depend on the mass of the black hole, scalar field strength, $λ$ and other positive parameter $r_ϕ$. in this case, we propose two possible behaviors: when the black hole's mass is small enough, the field is mostly concentrated far from the black hole, whereas when the black hole's mass is sufficiently large, it is mostly concentrated inside the black hole.

title: construction of causal set propagators in $2+1$-dimensional constant-curvature spacetimes from two-link paths
abstract: we study a link-based retarded scalar propagator on causal sets sprinkled into $2+1$-dimensional minkowski, anti-de sitter, and de sitter spacetimes. the construction is based on the squared link matrix $\mathbf{l}^2$, whose expectation value counts two-link paths between fixed endpoints. in the high-density limit, the dominant contribution localizes near the intersection of the null boundaries of the alexandrov interval, and the flat-space normalization remains unchanged in constant curvature. the resulting kernels agree with the corresponding continuum klein-gordon propagators for a nominally massless scalar with effective curvature coupling $ξ_{\rm link}=1/6$. since the conformal coupling in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions is $1/8$, this value is not a conformal-coupling effect. together with link-based results in $1+1$ and $3+1$ dimensions, where the same coefficient $1/6$ appears, this suggests that the coupling may reflect an ultraviolet property of the link structure, reminiscent of the combination $(1/6-ξ)\mathcal{r}$ in local heat-kernel expansions.

title: gravitational dark matter production in einstein-cartan theory
abstract: introducing torsion into general relativity leads to new four-point interactions for fermions. these are universal and must also affect any fermion dark matter. we improve existing calculations of dark matter production through the einstein-cartan theory four-fermion interaction by also considering the s-channel graviton exchange as another contributing process. the effect on both the total cross section as well as the momentum-dependent boltzmann equation collision term is calculated and discussed. we also introduce the holst term, which generally modifies the four-fermion interaction coupling constant as well as introduces two new four-fermion interactions, and discuss and compute its effect on the total produced dark matter abundance.

title: geodesics of the five-dimensional kerr-(a)ds black hole in closed form
abstract: the hamilton-jacobi equation for geodesic motion in the five-dimensional kerr-(a)ds black hole separates in boyer-lindquist coordinates, but the resulting first-order system has so far been integrated case by case, according to the real roots of the radial and the polar polynomial. we give the general solution in closed form. in dimensionless variables both polynomials are quartic, and a theorem of biermann and weierstrass then yields the radial and the polar coordinate as one pair of manifestly real formulas, parametrized by an arbitrary point of the orbit rather than by a turning point, and valid for timelike and null geodesics alike whatever the root structure. the time coordinate and the two azimuthal angles follow by quadratures that reduce to elliptic integrals of the third kind alone, and the affine parameter by one more of the same type. along the way we correct the inverse metric and the radial potential as published.

title: analog regular black holes and black hole mimickers in a bose-einstein condensate: from the core to the light rings
abstract: we show how static, spherically symmetric regular black holes and black-hole mimickers with radius-dependent mass function $m(r)$ can be emulated in a quasi-two-dimensional bose--einstein condensate, with the aim of probing inner-horizon and inner-light-ring instabilities in the laboratory. matching the acoustic and gravitational line elements on an equatorial disc fixes the ratio of radial flow velocity to sound speed and reproduces both horizon locations and surface gravities exactly. the analogue geometry nevertheless contains a residual radially varying sound-speed factor in $g_{tt}$, which shifts the light-ring positions and reduces the range of the regularization parameter $\ell/m$ for which a light-ring pair exists. we derive the interaction profile that removes this shift. combining the metric correspondence with the continuity and bernoulli equations, we then obtain closed-form expressions for the external potential and interaction strength realizing the full target spacetime, with $m$ and $\ell$ directly tunable through parameters of the potential. finally, we translate the construction into experimental requirements (quasi-two-dimensional confinement, healing-length resolution, three-body lifetime, and stationary-flow lifetime) and present three fiducial designs achievable with present-day $^{39}\mathrm{k}$ platforms.

title: u(1) current diffusion in gauss-bonnet holography
