abstract: we study holographic $u(1)$ charge transport using a probe maxwell field in a five-dimensional gauss-bonnet-ads black-brane background. within the all-order linearised fluid/gravity framework, we derive the off-shell constitutive relation and determine the diffusion function and electric and magnetic conductivities analytically in the hydrodynamic regime and numerically at generic frequency and momentum. to first order in the gauss-bonnet coupling, the leading diffusion constant remains unchanged in our normalization, while its frequency dependence and the electric conductivity receive nontrivial corrections. the deformation also generates a nonvanishing leading magnetic conductivity. beyond the hydrodynamic regime, it modifies the transport profiles while preserving the damped behaviour of the diffusion function. the corresponding memory kernel vanishes at negative times, supporting a retarded constitutive response.

title: gpu-accelerated bayesian inference for diffracted gravitational wave signals
abstract: as the rate of gravitational wave detections continues to grow, the probability of observing a gravitationally lensed gravitational wave also increases. when the schwarzschild radius of the lens is comparable in size to the gravitational wave wavelength, wave-optics effects induce a frequency- dependent modulation on the signal. cpu-based parameter estimation analyses for wave-optics lensing are computationally intensive, limiting the scale of studies to determine the significance of any potential lensing candidate. in this work, we implement a point-mass lens model in jim, a high-performance gpu-based parameter estimation pipeline. this enables, for the first time, gpu-accelerated bayesian inference in full-wave optics, including the computation of bayes factors, without the need for training data. we call this framework jim-lensing. using this framework, we are able to speed up a full parameter estimation run under the point-mass lens hypothesis from more than 10 hours to the order of 10 minutes compared to the current state-of-the-art cpu-based pipeline. we show that our implementation is stable and obtains comparable results to this state-of- the-art pipeline. the substantial speed gain over existing cpu pipelines paves the way for analyzing gravitational wave data under a broader range of lensing models with greater capacity to produce robust frequentist significance estimates.

title: cosmological perturbations from localized sources: a gauge-invariant multipolar theory
abstract: we develop a first-principles description of the linearized gravitational field of localized sources in spatially flat friedmann-lema\^ıtre-robertson-walker universes with arbitrary smooth expansion histories. the construction determines the complete retarded metric and the induced perturbation of the surrounding cosmic fluid from prescribed source stresses and a cosmologically stationary past field. it includes all multipole orders and accounts for curvature tails, through which the field depends on the source's past history inside the light cone. generalizing the blanchet-damour multipolar formalism, we identify gauge-invariant mass and current moments together with a canonical cosmic fluid moment that determines an independent scalar response. this response vanishes in minkowski and pure de sitter spacetime, although curvature tails persist in de sitter. the gauge-invariant multipoles are obtained directly in position space. this gives an exterior description without the nonlocal spatial projection through the source interior required by the usual scalar-vector-tensor decomposition. we also relate the canonical multipole metric to the standard variables of cosmological perturbation theory. the retarded construction requires neither a slow-motion nor a geometric-optics approximation. we define effective multipolar sources by truncating the moments of slowly varying sub-hubble extended sources at a prescribed cartesian multipole order, recovering the earlier quadrupolar and octupolar models in de sitter spacetime. we recover the known minkowski and de sitter multipolar fields and obtain an analytical representation for gravitational propagation in the $λ$cdm model including radiation.

title: a new class of rotating black hole solutions endowed with a scalar hair
abstract: we present new hairy stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions. these solutions belong to a subclass of horndeski scalar-tensor theories, in which there is no non-minimal coupling to curvature. the full rotating solutions are obtained numerically using the kadath library based on spectral methods. the metric does not rely on an explicit ansatz but rather on the use of a set of numerical coordinates. black holes obtained differ from kerr in general, and depend on a new independent parameter, a primary hair, coming from a linear time dependence in the scalar field. these solutions admit a killing horizon like the kerr black hole, but are non-circular, and break the zeroth law of black hole thermodynamics.

title: gravitational fingerprints of a black hole solution in palatini kalb-ramond gravity
abstract: we investigate particle motion, optical observables, and linear wave propagation around a static black hole in palatini kalb ramond gravity with a vanishing cosmological constant. the analysis distinguishes the conserved mass $m$ from the orbital mass $\bar{m}=m/ρ$ and isolates the radial deformation $σ^2=1-q/2$, where $q=\ell_2/(1-\ell_1)$. at fixed $\bar{m}$, the photon sphere, critical impact parameter, and innermost stable circular orbit retain their schwarzschild values. radial frequency ratios also preserve their schwarzschild profiles for the same areal release and particle radii, while proper distances, infall times, and accumulated orbital angles depend on $σ$. for radial fall, the tidal eigenvalues acquire a factor $σ^{-2}$, and the instability exponent of the photon orbit scales as $σ^{-1}$. in addition, we examine light deflection in the weak and strong regimes with an explicit account of the conical asymptotics. the shadow comparison with sgr a* and m87* exhibits a coupling degeneracy when the orbital mass and areal distance are set. scalar, electromagnetic, and massless dirac perturbations probe the physical metric, whereas a homogeneous axial gravitational sector with $δb_{μν}=0$ admits an exact schwarzschild spectral map. in this sector, both oscillation and attenuation rates scale as $σ^{-1}$ at fixed $\bar{m}$. third order wkb estimates agree with frequencies extracted from time evolution to within $0.7\%$ for the reported fundamental modes.

title: cosmological implications of two mock tianqin standard siren catalogs generated under different background cosmological models
abstract: space-borne gravitational wave (gw) detectors such as tianqin are expected to detect gw standard sirens for cosmological parameter estimation. all previous studies of tianqin adopted the $λ$cdm model to generate mock standard siren data. in this work, we quantitatively investigate how the choice of background cosmological model affects mock tianqin standard siren (tqss) catalogs and the corresponding cosmological implications. adopting the $λ$cdm model and a redshift-binned dark energy (de) reconstruction model (the wbin model), we consider the bright standard sirens from massive black hole binary mergers and generate two mock tqss catalogs, i.e. tqss1 and tqss2, respectively. we investigate the difference of the catalogs and further explore their cosmological implications within the chevallier-polarski-linder (cpl) model, both individually and in combination with desi dr2 baryon acoustic oscillation (bao) data, $\textit{planck}$ 2018 cosmic microwave background (cmb) data, and desy5 type ia supernova (sn ia) data. we find that there are only small differences between tqss1 and tqss2 catalogs, with a maximum relative difference of $1.48\%$ in the distance-redshift relation. in addition, either the tqss1 or tqss2 catalog alone gives cosmological constraints similar to those obtained from sn data, implying that these two catalogs can serve as a complement to mainstream cosmological observations. most importantly, we find that both tqss1+desi dr2+cmb+desy5 and tqss2+desi dr2+cmb+desy5 are still expected to favor dynamical de, with these two combinations showing a preference for dynamical de at $2.3σ$ and $3.8σ$, respectively. adopting different massive black hole seed models does not impact the cosmological implications of the mock tqss catalogs. our study indicates the importance of considering different cosmological models in the standard siren forecasts for de.

title: spherically symmetric solutions with dust and radiation sources in schouten-codazzi gravity
abstract: we examine in this paper exact solutions of schouten-codazzi gravity (scg), a second order metric theory in which a codazzi tensor is added to the einstein field equations. we consider two spherically symmetric geometries that describe null radiation and inhomogeneous dust, corresponding to generalized vaidya and lemaître-tolman-bondi (ltb) spacetimes. the codazzi tensor has to comply the codazzi equations, this imposes restrictions on the geometry of spacetime that are determined up to two integration functions that naturally generate an effective ``cosmological constant'' and an additional degree of freedom. we show that for the vaidya geometry, these codazzi contributions modify the misner-sharp mass, while the ltb models have as an evolution equation a cubic polynomial whose coefficients depend on the codazzi integration functions. this leads to a broader class of dynamics than those of general relativity, and allows for an accelerated expansion and ever-expanding models without the introduction of ``dark energy''. overall, our analysis suggests that schouten-codazzi gravity provides an appealing framework for applications in cosmology.
